ordered_diagnoses: FIP1L1-PDGFRA–positive chronic eosinophilic leukemia (CEL) with associated generalized eruptive histiocytosis (GEH)
Myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia and FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion

s1.syndrome_frame: a chronic skin condition with systemic involvement characterized by asymptomatic red to brown macules and papules, symmetrically distributed on the trunk and extremities, with associated laboratory abnormalities and histopathological findings
salient_findings: asymptomatic red to brown macules and papules on trunk and extremities
symmetric distribution of lesions without coalescence
elevated eosinophil count and tryptase level
nodular infiltration of histiocytes with lymphocytes and eosinophils in skin biopsy
key_facts: male patient in his 20s
12-month history of skin lesions
lesions initially appeared on trunk and spread to upper and proximal lower extremities
face, distal extremities, and mucous membranes unaffected
some lesions resolved spontaneously with residual hyperpigmentation
hypereosinophilia (4220/μL) on blood cell count
elevated tryptase (33.7 ng/mL)
elevated vitamin B12 (>6000 pg/mL)
negative serologic tests for HIV, hepatitis A, B, and C
negative tests for parasitic infections
skin biopsy showed nodular infiltration of histiocytes with lymphocytes and eosinophils
bone marrow analysis showed hypercellularity with myeloid hyperplasia and increased eosinophils
FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene positive on RT-PCR

raw.champion: FIP1L1-PDGFRA–positive chronic eosinophilic leukemia (CEL) with associated generalized eruptive histiocytosis (GEH)
raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of skin lesions, hypereosinophilia, elevated tryptase, and elevated vitamin B12, along with the presence of the FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene on RT-PCR and the specific findings on skin biopsy and bone marrow analysis, are all consistent with FIP1L1-PDGFRA-positive CEL, and the skin manifestations are suggestive of associated GEH.

rejected.label: Myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia and FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion
rejected.why: While the FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion is present, the specific constellation of findings, including the skin manifestations and the bone marrow analysis, are more consistent with FIP1L1-PDGFRA-positive CEL with GEH.

rejected.label: Idiopathic hypereosinophilic syndrome
rejected.why: The presence of the FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene and the specific findings on skin biopsy and bone marrow analysis suggest a more specific diagnosis than idiopathic hypereosinophilic syndrome.

rejected.label: Histiocytosis with eosinophilia
rejected.why: While histiocytosis is present, the overall clinical and laboratory picture, including the FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion, is more consistent with FIP1L1-PDGFRA-positive CEL with GEH.

rejected.label: Mastocytosis
rejected.why: The lack of mast cell infiltration on skin biopsy and the presence of the FIP1L1-PDGFRA fusion gene make mastocytosis an unlikely diagnosis.
